column1: # tests/lever-reachability-exempt.tsv — the opt-out list for the INERT-LEVER guard (HERD-556,
# scripts/herd/lever-reachability-lint.sh).
# Format: <CONFIG_KEY><TAB><reason>. Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. The reason is
# MANDATORY — a bare row reds as EXEMPT-MALFORMED rather than silently laundering a finding, because
# a row here is a DECISION on the record, not a silencer.
# A row is also RED once it goes STALE: if the key stops being a finding (its consumer chain became
# reachable, or the key was removed), the guard reports STALE-EXEMPT and the row must go. An
# exemption list that outlives the thing it excused is how a ratchet quietly stops ratcheting.
# TWO KINDS OF ROW, and the difference matters:
#   INTENTIONAL — a lever that is unreachable under the shipped engine ON PURPOSE (a bash-only knob
#   kept for a consuming project, a documented latent lever). The reason says why a future auditor
#   should NOT re-wire it. There are none yet.
#   BASELINE (HERD-556) — a lever that was ALREADY inert when this guard first ran, on 2026-08-05.
#   These are real findings, not exemptions: each is filed for the coordinator via `herd note` and is
#   deliberately NOT fixed in the guard's own PR (fixing eight levers blind, in the change that first
#   made them visible, is how a lint PR turns into an outage). They are listed so the guard ships
#   GREEN and works as a NO-NEW-INERT-LEVER ratchet from day one; the ADVISORY line keeps the count
#   visible ("N exempt (M silencing a finding)") so the debt cannot fade into the background. Remove
#   a row when its item lands — the STALE-EXEMPT rule above will insist.
# The five BASELINE rows this file used to carry (GATE_DISPATCH, DELTA_REVIEW, WATCH_CLAUDE_PROBE_TIMEOUT,
# REVIEW_MODEL_ESCALATED, REVIEW_EVIDENCE_ESCALATE_ROUNDS — epic HERD-561 children 3-6) were the same
# incident: the P5b engine port (HERD-306) moved gate dispatch into pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py and the
# bash gate pass lost its caller, so each key's only consumer hung off the dead `_review_gate_step` /
# `_predispatch_review_if_parallel` and changed nothing. HERD-580 closed every one: GATE_DISPATCH was
# RETIRED (its bash body deleted — no lever the Python port never implemented is worth keeping around);
# the other four were PORTED into pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's live review dispatch, so each now has a
# real python-side consumer and no longer needs an exemption row.
